scope.notificationLocators: Physiotherapy syllabus pp. 97–99; illustrative sample begins Annexure B p. 106

method: Loaded every record from all nine durable group files and the merged file; checked the unchanged ten-field question schema, section, canonical topic, difficulty, four unique options, correct-index range, non-empty text/explanation/sourceId, and full-row merge equality.

Compared the bank against the Physiotherapy headings and subheadings in the SAI notification, including explicit component coverage within combined headings such as cardiovascular/pulmonary/gastrointestinal and massage/yoga.

Calculated exact and near-duplicate stems, answer-index counts, contiguous/repeating answer-position sequences, option-length spreads, correct-option longest/shortest rates, and correct-option versus distractor-median length differences.
Resolved every used sourceId against the source catalog and checked title, organization or authors, location, scope and locator metadata.

Manually re-read the 26 central factual-remediation records, including b-physiology-043 and the named sports-medicine remaps, against the cited local book, official document or official web source where applicable. Automated text overlap was used only as a screening aid, not as factual proof.

internalRepositorySubtopics.note: The internal group/subtopic allocation is populated, but this does not by itself prove coverage of every component named in the official syllabus.

officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.heading: Human Anatomy
officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.evidence: The anatomy group contains dedicated terminology, osteology/arthrology, limb/pelvis/spine, peripheral-nerve/dermatome and systemic-anatomy subtopics.

officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.heading: Human Physiology
officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.evidence: Homeostasis/fluid, blood, nerve/muscle, cardiorespiratory, renal, endocrine and thermoregulation records are present. The group has no substantive gastrointestinal physiology item, no dedicated reproductive physiology item, and no special-senses physiology item; central/autonomic coverage is only indirect/thin.

officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.heading: Exercise Physiology
officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.evidence: Cardiorespiratory responses, VO2/thresholds, fatigue/recovery, metabolic responses, environmental physiology and training adaptations are represented.

officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.heading: Electrotherapy and Electrodiagnosis
officialAreas: SWD, ultrasound, UVR, IRR, IFT, LASER, shockwave and cryotherapy
officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.evidence: All six official areas have dedicated internal subtopics and records, including the named modalities and strength-duration/rheobase content.

officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.heading: Exercise Therapy and Rehabilitation
officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.evidence: Exercise prescription, progression, kinetic-chain, stretching, PNF, strengthening, hydrotherapy, massage and functional retraining are represented. No yoga question or yoga concept was found in the Section B bank.

officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.heading: Biomechanics and Movement Analysis
officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.evidence: All six official areas have dedicated biomechanical subtopics and records.

officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.heading: Psychology and Human Development
officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.evidence: Motivation, self-efficacy, anxiety/stress, attention, mental skills, adherence, safeguarding and youth development records cover the three official areas.

officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.heading: Assessment, Diagnosis and Clinical Reasoning
officialAreas: movement, cardiovascular, pulmonary and musculoskeletal dysfunction
officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.evidence: Subjective/objective examination, ROM, manual testing, special tests, manual therapy, neurodynamics, movement/MSK assessment, pain and outcome measures are present. No substantive cardiovascular or pulmonary assessment record was found in this group.

officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.heading: Sports Physiotherapy
officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.evidence: Injury mechanisms, rehabilitation, emergencies, screening, non-traumatic/environmental conditions and team travel are represented. No body-composition, anthropometry, skinfold, BMI or body-composition-assessment question was found anywhere in Section B.

officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.heading: Sports Medicine, Nutrition and Research
officialAreas: doping and introduction to sports medicine
officialPhysiotherapyHeadings.evidence: The group includes sports-medicine roles/injury prevention, anti-doping/TUE/NADA, nutrition/hydration/supplements and research/statistics/ethics/data-governance records.

b-physiology-043.reason: The explanation correctly describes calcium-mediated force summation and explicitly preserves ATP use. The supplied Physiology of Sport and Exercise PDF discusses summation/tetanus and rate coding at PDF p. 69 and defines tetanus at PDF p. 612.

namedRecentRemediations.b-sportsmed-043: Answer is safe and unambiguous; source-scope limitation is recorded below.
namedRecentRemediations.b-sportsmed-044: Answer is safe and unambiguous; source-scope limitation is recorded below.
namedRecentRemediations.b-sportsmed-050: Answer is safe and unambiguous; source-scope limitation is recorded below.

namedSportsMedicineItems.evidence: WADA Code Article 21.1.3–21.1.4 directly supports athlete responsibility for what is used and for ensuring medical treatment does not violate anti-doping rules.
namedSportsMedicineItems.reviewFlag: The catalog locator lists Articles 2.1, 2.2 and 18 but should also identify Article 21.1.4.

namedSportsMedicineItems.evidence: WHO key messages support safe medication practice, shared decision-making and obtaining medication information from a health worker.
namedSportsMedicineItems.reviewFlag: The option adds anti-doping review, which is not directly covered by the cited WHO medication-safety page.

namedSportsMedicineItems.evidence: WHO directly recommends keeping an up-to-date medication list and sharing it with treating health workers.
namedSportsMedicineItems.reviewFlag: The explanation additionally claims anti-doping checking; that clause is not directly established by the WHO page.

namedSportsMedicineItems.evidence: The answer is consistent with safe, individualized medication use and health-worker oversight.
namedSportsMedicineItems.reviewFlag: The explanation adds that a shared medicine may be prohibited for another athlete; that anti-doping proposition is not directly established by the cited WHO page.

nearDuplicatePairs.note: Both ask which structure is assessed by the ankle anterior-drawer test and key the anterior talofibular ligament.
Both define sensitivity as the positive-test proportion among people with the condition.
Both define specificity as the negative-test proportion among people without the condition.

answerIndexAndOptionLengthReview.interpretation: Global counts are balanced, but group/topic-filtered tests expose deterministic answer positions. This is a release-blocking answer-pattern giveaway and must be independently randomized while preserving keys.

optionLengthReview.interpretation: The correct option is not systematically longest: longest and shortest rates remain below 35%, and only 19 records have the correct option at least ten characters longer than the distractor median. The 115 wide-spread sets merit editorial review but are not, by themselves, release blockers.

blockingDefects.details: Human Anatomy and Electrotherapy use an exact four-position sequence across all 150 records; Psychology and Assessment use an exact four-position sequence for their first 149 records. The pattern is predictable in topic-filtered practice and defeats the intended answer-position balancing review.
blockingDefects.requiredDisposition: Reorder options with a non-periodic, seeded distribution, then rerun key correctness and answer-balance audits.

blockingDefects.details: The bank does not substantively cover all components of the official Physiotherapy syllabus. Confirmed gaps are gastrointestinal physiology; reproductive physiology; special-senses physiology; yoga basics; cardiovascular/pulmonary dysfunction assessment; and body-composition assessment.
blockingDefects.requiredDisposition: Add or replace questions within the existing 150-question group limits so each named official component has defensible coverage, then rerun the independent coverage audit.

nonBlockingReviewFlags.details: Answers are defensible, but the WADA locator should identify Article 21.1.4 and the WHO source does not directly support the anti-doping clauses added to three medication items.
Three cross-group concept pairs are substantively duplicated even though their literal normalized stems differ.

b-exercise-093 has a 40-character option spread caused by an overqualified distractor; b-biomechanics-088 has the grammatically incomplete keyed option 'Raises body for opposite foot clearance'. The wider 115-item spread set should be reviewed in the same editorial pass.

pass: Exactly nine canonical durable groups and exactly 150 records per group.
Merged bank contains exactly 1,350 records and matches the canonical durable files row-for-row.
Schema, four-option uniqueness, valid zero-based keys, section values, difficulty values, duplicate IDs and exact duplicate stems pass.
All 40 used source IDs resolve and have catalog metadata sufficient to identify organization/authors, location, scope and locator.
b-physiology-043 has a corrected key and a source-supported calcium-summation explanation.
The manually reviewed factual remediations have no remaining answer-key contradiction or ambiguous key; remaining issues are provenance or editorial flags.
Overall answer-index counts are balanced and correct-option length metrics are below the configured longest-answer risk threshold.

recommendedDisposition: Do not claim release-ready status until the deterministic answer-position sequences are removed.
Close the six confirmed official-syllabus component gaps within the nine existing group files without changing the 150-per-group contract.
Then resolve the source-scope/locator flags, remove or differentiate the three near-duplicate pairs, and rerun structural, factual, coverage, provenance and answer-pattern audits.
